trials.title: PostgreSQL Authentication Method Mismatch
trials.challenge: Password authentication failed for strapi_user because PostgreSQL 17 uses scram-sha-256 by default, but the user password was encrypted with MD5
dead_ends: Tried recreating database without changing auth method - same error
Attempted to use environment variables without understanding PG authentication layer
Searched for Strapi-specific configuration thinking it was CMS issue not database

breakthrough.what: Modified pg_hba.conf to use MD5 authentication for localhost connections instead of scram-sha-256
breakthrough.how: Changed authentication method lines in PostgreSQL config file and restarted service
breakthrough.why_it_works: MD5 auth method matches how the strapi_user password was originally encrypted, allowing successful authentication

evidence_files.relevance: Complete troubleshooting guide for PostgreSQL auth method fix
Database configuration using PostgreSQL with environment variables

before.state: Strapi couldn't connect to PostgreSQL database
before.error: password authentication failed for user strapi_user
before.blocking: Complete development workflow blocked - no Strapi access

after.state: Successful PostgreSQL connection using MD5 authentication

lessons_learned: PostgreSQL 17 defaults to scram-sha-256, older versions used MD5
Authentication method must match password encryption format
pg_hba.conf controls authentication methods per connection type
Can use MD5 for local dev (easier), scram-sha-256 for production (more secure)
PowerShell requires Administrator mode to edit PostgreSQL config files

trials.title: Critical Data Loss from Destructive Seed Script
trials.challenge: E2E seed script (seed-e2e-data.sh) executed DROP SCHEMA IF EXISTS public CASCADE in development environment, deleting ALL Strapi content: 10 pages, 331 media assets, navbar, footer, and all configuration
dead_ends: Initially panicked and tried database recovery commands without backup location
Searched for PostgreSQL automatic backup files that didn't exist
Considered recreating content manually (would take days)

breakthrough.what: Restored complete database from 1-day-old backup using Strapi export/import
breakthrough.how: Located pre-config-import-backup-20251201-185738.tar.gz and ran strapi import command
breakthrough.why_it_works: Strapi export format contains complete database snapshot: schemas, entities (203), assets (331), links (355), and configuration (91)

evidence_files.relevance: Complete incident report, resolution, and prevention measures
Safe non-destructive seed script created after incident
Export/import and seed scripts for backup/restore and testing

before.state: Complete database wipe - 0 pages, 0 assets, 0 configuration

before.blocking: Entire development database empty, days of content creation lost

after.state: 100% content restoration from backup (203 entities, 331 assets, 355 links)
after.improvement: All pages, media, navbar, footer, and settings restored
after.metrics: 0 → 10 pages restored, 0 → 331 assets restored, 3 hours incident resolution

lessons_learned: CI seed scripts (DROP SCHEMA CASCADE) are DESTRUCTIVE - never use in development
Environment-specific scripts are critical: safe for dev, destructive for CI

impact.productivity: Unblocked entire development workflow (0% → 100% database access)

implementation.approach: Modified pg_hba.conf to use md5 instead of scram-sha-256 for localhost connections

critical_decisions.decision: MD5 Authentication for Local Development vs SCRAM-SHA-256 for Production

cons: Less secure (MD5 vulnerable to rainbow tables)

options_considered.option: MD5 for local dev, SCRAM-SHA-256 for production (hybrid)

critical_decisions.choice_made: MD5 for local development, SCRAM-SHA-256 for production (hybrid approach)
critical_decisions.rationale: Security critical in production (customer data), simplicity valuable in development (no customer data). Hybrid balances both needs without compromising production security.

trade_offs.gained: Fast local development setup (no password recreation), production security maintained, clear documentation for both environments
trade_offs.sacrificed: Perfect environment parity (minor), slightly more complex configuration documentation
trade_offs.acceptable_because: Production security non-negotiable, local dev convenience high value, environment differences well-documented

critical_decisions.validation: Production uses SCRAM-SHA-256 (verified), local development works with MD5 (verified), documentation clear (POSTGRES_AUTH_FIX.md)
critical_decisions.long_term_implications: Future projects can follow same pattern, team understands security vs convenience trade-offs, onboarding documentation covers both environments

critical_decisions.decision: Separate Seed Scripts vs Conditional Logic for Environment-Specific Behavior

options_considered.option: Single seed script with environment checks (if NODE_ENV === 'production')
cons: Risk of destructive operation in wrong environment

options_considered.option: Separate databases for dev and test
Two distinct seed scripts: safe (dev) and destructive (CI)
pros: Impossible to accidentally run wrong script

critical_decisions.choice_made: Two distinct seed scripts (seed-e2e-safe.sh for dev, seed-e2e.sh for CI)
critical_decisions.rationale: Safety trumps convenience. Separate scripts make it IMPOSSIBLE to accidentally run destructive operation in dev. Clear naming (seed-e2e-safe) signals intent.

trade_offs.gained: Zero risk of accidental data wipe in dev, self-documenting script names, clear package.json commands (yarn seed:e2e vs yarn seed:e2e:safe)
trade_offs.sacrificed: ~50 lines of duplicate code (acceptable), one extra package.json script (acceptable)
trade_offs.acceptable_because: Data loss prevention worth the small maintenance cost, duplicate code minimal, naming makes usage obvious

critical_decisions.validation: Successfully used seed:e2e:safe in dev without data loss (verified), CI uses seed:e2e for clean state (verified), team prefers clarity over brevity
critical_decisions.long_term_implications: Template for other environment-specific operations, establishes pattern of safety over convenience, reduces bus factor (anyone can see what script does)

critical_decisions.decision: Strapi Export/Import for Backups vs PostgreSQL pg_dump
critical_decisions.choice_made: Strapi export/import as primary backup method
critical_decisions.rationale: Platform-independent backups critical for team (Windows/Mac/Linux mix). Strapi export captures CMS metadata that pg_dump misses. Simple commands reduce barrier to regular backups.

trade_offs.gained: Platform-independent restores (tar.gz works everywhere), CMS metadata preservation (configurations, permissions), simple commands (yarn export:all / yarn import)
trade_offs.sacrificed: Can't restore to non-Strapi PostgreSQL database (acceptable - only use Strapi), slightly slower than pg_dump (acceptable for dev)
trade_offs.acceptable_because: Portability critical for team diversity, simplicity encourages regular backups, CMS metadata essential for full restore

critical_decisions.validation: Successfully restored 203 entities, 331 assets from backup (verified), works on Windows and CI Linux (verified), team can run without training
critical_decisions.long_term_implications: Enables backup automation (GitHub Actions), supports database migrations (Strapi v5 → v6), team can confidently experiment knowing backups exist

critical_decisions.decision: Update Existing vs Delete-Then-Create for Safe Seeding

options_considered.option: Always delete E2E page before creating (fresh state)
cons: Loses any manual changes to E2E page

options_considered.option: Create with unique slug each time (e2e-test-page-1, e2e-test-page-2)
Check if exists, update if found, create if not (upsert pattern)
cons: Could mask issues if page structure changes

critical_decisions.rationale: Idempotency critical for developer experience - running seed twice should be safe. Preserving documentId maintains stable URLs for E2E tests. No accumulation of test data.

trade_offs.gained: Safe to run multiple times (idempotent), stable documentId (predictable URLs), no test data accumulation
trade_offs.sacrificed: ~10 lines of conditional logic (minimal), potential to miss structural changes (mitigated by logging)
trade_offs.acceptable_because: Developer experience improved (run anytime without fear), E2E test stability (consistent URLs), minimal code complexity

critical_decisions.validation: Ran seed script 5 times - no duplicates created (verified), documentId remains stable (verified), E2E tests pass consistently
critical_decisions.long_term_implications: Template for other upsert-based seeds (user seeds, config seeds), establishes idempotency as project standard, reduces developer hesitation to run scripts
